takeaway: Ewing's sarcoma: a young person with a hot, hard swelling and an onion-skin lesion in the medulla of a long bone.

question.text: A 16-year-old boy has right upper arm pain with no trauma and a hot, hard swelling. X-ray: an onion-skin lesion in the medulla of the humerus. What is the diagnosis?
question.say: A sixteen-year-old boy has right upper arm pain with no trauma, and a hot, hard swelling. The X-ray shows an onion-skin lesion in the medulla of the humerus. What is the diagnosis?

lines.text: A 16-year-old boy with a hot, hard swelling in his arm.
lines.say: This sixteen-year-old boy has pain in his right upper arm, with a hot, hard swelling in the middle of it.

lines.text: There was no trauma: the banana skin is crossed out.
lines.say: There is no history of trauma, so the banana skin is crossed out.

lines.text: The X-ray shows an onion-skin lesion in the medulla of the humerus.
lines.say: (laugh) And the X-ray shows an onion in the bone. This onion-skin lesion sits in the medulla of the humerus.

lines.text: That is Ewing's sarcoma, a rare malignant bone tumour.
lines.say: That is Ewing's sarcoma, a rare malignant bone tumour of the medullary cavity.

lines.text: More common in males, with a peak between 10 and 20 years.
lines.say: It is more common in males, with a peak between ten and twenty years.

lines.text: Remember: an onion-skin lesion in the medulla of a teenager's bone means Ewing's sarcoma.
lines.say: Remember: an onion-skin lesion in the medulla of a teenager's bone means Ewing's sarcoma.
